verified.exploit_entry_point: The real Yamcs server started in-process by the project's own integration harness (YamcsServer.start(), port 9190, the HiddenIT configuration derived from the project's IntegrationTest config), driven by the real yamcs-client over a real websocket (topics packets, containers, stream, mdb-changes, algorithm-status, commands) and by the generated REST method descriptors (MdbOverrideApiClient, TableApiClient). Each test signs in as its own role-scoped user on its own client, because the websocket handshake captures the authenticated user. All expectations are computed in the tests.
sites: yamcs-core/src/main/java/org/yamcs/http/api/PacketsApi.java:499-527 subscribePackets(processor): per-item ReadPacket filtering of delivered packets (published fix)
yamcs-core/src/main/java/org/yamcs/http/api/TableApi.java:177-199 subscribeStream: ReadTables system privilege (pattern B, real upstream)
yamcs-core/src/main/java/org/yamcs/http/api/MdbOverrideApi.java:55-82 listMdbOverrides: GetMissionDatabase system privilege (pattern B, real upstream)
yamcs-core/src/main/java/org/yamcs/http/api/MdbOverrideApi.java:118-136 getAlgorithmOverrides: GetMissionDatabase or ReadAlgorithm (pattern B, real upstream)
routes: WebSocket topic stream (TableApi.subscribeStream) delivers packet-bearing tuples gated only by the stream object privilege; confirmed on the pinned+injected tree: a stream-object-only user receives rows
REST listMdbOverrides and getAlgorithmOverrides return override data with no check; confirmed on the pinned+injected tree: a user with no privileges receives a successful response
verified.project_tests_run: tests/src/test/java/org/yamcs/tests/PermissionsTest.java: 5 tests, compiled and run online during the image build, all pass. Hidden suite: 9 security + 9 functional; on the pinned+injected code all 9 security tests fail and all 9 functional tests pass; on the oracle all 18 pass.
verified.probe: 2026-10-19: probe subscriptions on the pinned tree confirmed the delivered packet name is the root sequence-container name (/REFMDB/ccsds-default) for every processor packet, and that every protected subscription/REST read succeeds for an unprivileged user. present_in_latest was read from current upstream: MdbOverrideApi now filters its list/read per object (no longer exposed), TableApi.subscribeStream still has no ReadTables check.

wrong_resource: the generic stream subscription checks the neighbouring stream object privilege instead of the table-read privilege; the attacker holds the stream privilege
refuse_all: the live packet feed demands the table-read privilege, so a caller authorized for the delivered packet name loses the feed
adjacent_api: the shared stream verifier requires the table-read privilege, breaking the ordinary stream description for a stream-object user
oracle plus per-item filtering inside the container listener and a control privilege on processor statistics; scores 1.0
independent correct fix: direct object/system privilege checks that throw, an early-return consumer filter, a per-name container loop, and the check placed after the stream verification; scores 1.0
informed control written with the trap list (agent version, per-packet archived-name check); adopted 2026-10-20 when the packet-feed rule moved to option A

patch_checks.why: wrong_resource (upstream-style fix): the live processor packet feed is authorised on the subscribed root container's name instead of each packet's archived name; a caller with ReadPacket on the root name receives every packet, and a caller authorized for a subset receives nothing (2026-10-20, option A)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the tests accept any client error and no assertion distinguishes a crash from a refusal; no product path panics on these inputs
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: every affected operation is a read and authorization is evaluated per authenticated caller; there is no second role, peer or direction on these paths
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: all affected operations are reads; the write counterparts already require ChangeMissionDatabase or ModifyCommandHistory and are unchanged
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no adjustment or normalisation sits between the request value and the authorization decision
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: objects are addressed by exact qualified names or a stream name; there is no parser or alias spelling that changes which object is checked
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the role store always yields a defined (possibly empty) privilege set for an authenticated user; there is no fail-open when a secret or role record is absent

traps.shape: the reported sink: live packet subscription with a processor must filter each delivered packet by the caller's ReadPacket privilege instead of streaming everything The per-packet check uses the name each packet is archived under (the name the ordinary packet reads authorise), not the subscribed container's name (2026-10-20).
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the site the report points at

traps.shape: the second input shape of the same request: raw-stream packet subscription must require the table-read system privilege; the stream object check looks sufficient
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the stream is already gated by a stream object privilege, so a reader assumes the data is protected

traps.shape: far site in another file: mission-database change notifications must require the mission-database system privilege
traps.reason_to_dismiss: override notifications look like metadata rather than packet data, and the file is not the one the report names

traps.shape: far site in another file: live algorithm status must apply the per-algorithm read privilege
traps.reason_to_dismiss: algorithm status is diagnostic metadata, and its object privilege is easy to miss next to the system privileges used by the other processor endpoints

traps.shape: real upstream route to the same packet-bearing data: the generic stream subscription must require the table-read system privilege like the packet subscription's stream branch
traps.reason_to_dismiss: its ordinary REST sibling uses exactly the same stream-object gate, so it appears to match REST and to be protected

traps.shape: real upstream routes to the same protected data: the ordinary readers that list all active overrides and read one algorithm's override text enforce nothing while their sibling readers/writers do
traps.reason_to_dismiss: they are ordinary REST routes and the report leads to the subscription side; the REST side is assumed to be the guarded side
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (upstream later changed these readers to per-object filtering)

traps.shape: the container subscription has no request-time ReadPacket check, so a caller can request any named container's bytes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a separate narrow subscription with explicit names; fixing the reported packet feed looks like it covers the same bytes
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling in our copy only; a maintainer could plausibly have written this endpoint without the check, relying on the packet subscription's guard

traps.shape: the command-history subscription filters the creation callback per command but emits every update entry with no CommandHistory check
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the update callback is assumed to carry only attribute changes while the creation callback carries the command content
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling in our copy only; the two callbacks are written separately, so the second can plausibly be left without the check the first one has
